newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil gas lines upgrade ahead of plan.
newsitem.headline: Statoil gas lines upgrade ahead of plan.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday a project to expand gas export capacity through the gas pipelines from the Kollsnes terminal near Bergen to Europe was ahead of schedule.

The work was due to be completed in October, but was expected to be finished roughly two months ahead of schedule. The additional time would be used for testing, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.

The project involved upgrading the Kollsnes compressor plant to boost export pressure in the Zeepipe IIA and IIB pipelines from 167 to 190 bar. Statoil said this would increase capacity be about 40 percent.
Raising export pressure in Zeepipe IIB also enhances capacity in Europipe I, making it possible to postpone installation of the Europipe II gas trunkline by one year.

Norway's parliament in December approved plans for Europipe II, which is now planned to begin operation in October 1999. The 635 km (395 mile) line will run from Kaarstoe, north of Stavanger, to Germany.
Statoil said the expansion project used new technology and cost-effective solutions, including a recently developed system to protect against excess pressure in pipelines.
The company is able to monitor the entire system from Kollsnes by using satellites to transmit back metering results measured at the opposite ends of the lines.
